narration.opening: This is Eterna: the control layer for agents that pay across networks.
narration.problem: Rose is a CFO. Her agents pay with vouchers, cards and ledgers. Each system checks its own piece — nobody checks the whole mission against what she approved.
narration.solution: Rose approves one mission: one task, one seller, a per-payment limit, a total budget and an expiry. Eterna turns it into a signed certificate. On the XRP Ledger, delegation gives her agent only the permission it needs, and sponsorship covers its network costs.
narration.transaction: The seller asks for payment with an HTTP 402. Eterna checks the request against Rose's mission, and only then does the agent sign a voucher. These vouchers come from our local simulator of Mastercard's Agent Pay model — not from Mastercard. The seller verifies each voucher and serves the report.
narration.proof: Every part keeps its own label. The sponsorship, the delegation and the settlement are verified on XRPL Devnet. The vouchers are simulated. Eterna links all of it into one audit receipt, anchored on the ledger.
narration.outcome: The reports unlock only after Eterna has checked the settlement on the ledger. A request outside Rose's mission was refused before anything was signed.
narration.closing: One authorization. Multiple payments. Verifiable proof.
